partially_covered.missing: Organization and Address classes remain, but still lack explicit properties for legal name, registration number, contact info, etc. Only address lines and identifiers are present.
Item class still lacks detailed attributes (e.g., item description, SKU, unit of measure). Only price and quantity are modeled.

Invoice details are distributed across sections, but no explicit summary or grouping property for overall invoice details. Document date and reference number are present in header, but not aggregated.

cq_coverage.details: Coverage remains high for most CQs, with main gaps still in organization and item details, and invoice detail aggregation. No new CQs were fully addressed since last iteration.

strengths: Deep, well-structured class hierarchy reflecting EDIFACT and business document structure
Comprehensive use of property characteristics and restrictions
weaknesses: No General Class Axioms (GCAs) or owl:equivalentClass for complex definitions
No enrichment for detailed item or organization attributes
No explicit union/disjoint union constructs for Section subclasses

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4 (Missing domain/range for some properties — minor, but not observed in this version)
P7 (No equivalence axioms for key classes)
reasoner_risks: Hermit/Pellet may slow on complex restrictions but no datatype or structural violations detected

summary: The ontology maintains a high level of structural quality, OWL 2 compliance, and annotation completeness. However, none of the recommended improvements from the previous review were implemented—coverage and quality remain static, with persistent gaps in organization/item detail and advanced axiomatization. Progress is fair, and further enrichment is needed for full CQ coverage and semantic depth.
